summary.lead: Official summary (Congressional Research Service, Introduced in House):

blocks.text: This bill requires the Forest Service to convey approximately 14 acres of federal land, including the mineral rights, in the Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest, Wisconsin, to Tony's Wabeno Redi-Mix, LLC, upon receiving an offer to buy the land for market value.

The Forest Service must complete an appraisal to determine the market value of the land, and the offer must be received within 180 days after federal approval of such appraisal. Tony's Wabeno Redi-Mix, LLC, must pay an amount equal to the market value of the land and all associated costs as a condition of conveyance.
Additionally, the Department of the Interior must publish a comprehensive review of the federal permitting processes for the development of stone, sand, and gravel on federal lands.

The Wabeno Economic Development Act would require the Forest Service to sell about 14 acres of federal land in the Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest in Wisconsin, along with the minerals underneath it, to Tony's Wabeno Redi-Mix, LLC. The sale would go ahead only if the company makes an offer to buy the land.

The Forest Service would first have to determine the land's market value through an appraisal. The company would need to submit its offer within 180 days after federal approval of that appraisal. As a condition of the sale, the company would have to pay the full market value of the land plus all costs connected to the transfer.
The bill also would require the Department of the Interior to publish a comprehensive review of the federal permitting processes used to develop stone, sand, and gravel on federal lands.
